reader.requirement: At --std 85 every report group description entry must begin with a level-number, a one- or two-digit number (1 through 9 also as 01 through 09, IV.7.4), whose value under an RD is 01 through 49 only (XIII.3.14.3 SR2); single-digit and two-digit spellings across that range must be accepted and build the group hierarchy, and 0, 50, 66, 77, 88, a three-digit spelling and an entry with no level-number must be refused. The witness covers only a legal hierarchy.

edition-consulted.switches: refuses a 2002 constant entry (01 ... CONSTANT AS) below 2002, including one standing in the REPORT SECTION, which LevelNumberPass.Classify leaves to the constant-entry binder

reader.edition-search: grep Edition/Dialect/CobolVersion in LevelNumberPass.cs: none (the pass takes only a diagnostic sink, so the report-group arm, the 1-49 range and the two-digit test are the same at every edition)

reader.notes: LevelNumberPass classifies a reportGroupEntry's level-number to the ReportGroup arm (1-49, no specials) and refuses any spelling over two digits; the pass consults no edition, which is right because 1985 states the same range and spelling. A first probe of mine wrote 49 and 09 as siblings and drew COBOL2771, which is correct at 85 (§1985 data division concepts require identical level-numbers for items immediately subordinate to a group).

refuter.evidence: At --std 85, against what the reader did not probe: l1 an RD whose first entry is 05 (GR1: 01 identifies the first entry) -> COBOL2772 'report group entry before any 01-level entry' plus COBOL2247; l2 levels 01/05/03 in one group -> COBOL2771 unequal subordinate levels; l3 01 DETAIL with two 05 LINE groups of 07 items, plus a level-01 REPORT FOOTING with a level-49 item -> report '007/AB/007/AB/ /END'; l5 05 indented two columns into area A -> runs; l6 a format-2 05 LINE entry with nothing subordinate -> COBOL2247 (§1985:XIII.3.9.3 SR4c). Class c: l4 level 01 under RD written in area B -> COBOL3734 'requires COBOL-2002' at 85 (§1985:IV.7.4 requires 01 in area A), the same source runs at --std 2023 ('007/007'). cite.py: OK §1985:XIII.3.14.4 GR1; OK §1985:XIII.3.14.3 SR2; OK §1985:IV.7.4 (01 or 77 must begin in area A).
